entries.lesson_title: Convolution of Two Equal-Width Rectangular Pulses
entries.core_move: Compute the continuous-time convolution of two equal-width rectangular pulses by tracking the moving overlap interval and converting its length into the resulting piecewise triangular waveform.

Compute the convolution of unequal-width rectangular pulses by identifying the edge-aligned breakpoints, expressing the sliding overlap length piecewise, and scaling by the pulse amplitudes to obtain the trapezoidal output.
Construct the triangular convolution output for rectangular pulses by using the overlap interval to compute the linearly increasing and decreasing overlap area across each time region.
Compute trapezoidal outputs from unequal-width rectangular-pulse convolution by partitioning time into no-overlap, growing-overlap, full-overlap, and shrinking-overlap regions.

entries.lesson_title: Geometric Area Methods for Rectangular Pulse Convolution
entries.core_move: Compute rectangular-pulse convolutions by translating overlap intervals into geometric areas that produce the correct triangular or trapezoidal piecewise output across time.
